newsitem.title: CHINA: Esprit seeks venture partners in China.
newsitem.headline: Esprit seeks venture partners in China.

text.p: Fashion distributor and wholesaler Esprit Asia Ltd chairman Michael Ying said on Tuesday Esprit is looking for joint venture partners in China to develop its business in the country.
"We are in talks with several parties but the discussions are in a very preliminary stage," Ying told reporters after a lease signing ceremony with Swire Pacific group.
He said Esprit was seeking partners with local experience such as its July joint venture in Japan with Taka-Q Co Ltd to set up a 50-50 venture for selling women's and children's clothing.
"Once we find suitable place in Japan, we will start (business)," Ying said.

But the chairman dismissed market rumours that Esprit was being targetted by a Chinese company for taking a stake in the firm. "So far no Chinese companies approached us on possible acquisition of shares," he said.
Esprit has about 100 outlets in China and plans to open another 100 in the coming 12 to 18 months.
Ying also said the Hong Kong retail market continued to be sluggish in the second half of 1997.
Esprit managed to maintain its profit margin in the first half of the year, he said.
"But there was no growth in market shares," he said.
Esprit has signed a lease contract with Swire group to open a 12,000 square feet flagship store at the Festival Walk retail and commercial centre at Yau Yat Tsuen in Kowloon Peninsula.
"We will take a more aggressive strategy next year after holding back a bit this year," he said. The shopping centre was expected to open in the summer of 1998.
